edbDesc: The process of forcing a solvent from a region of high solute concentration through a semipermeable membrane to a region of low solute concentration by applying a pressure in excess of the osmotic pressure. The result is that the solute is retained on the pressurized side of the membrane and the pure solvent is allowed to pass to the other side. It is most often applied as a filter.
title: Reverse Osmosis
pickWhy: Borderline: Judgment call: reverse osmosis is osmosis driven backward by pressure, so it counts as the deck's Osmosis card, with desalination as a use; a separate keep (Loeb and Sourirajan's 1960 membrane) is defensible since it is the famous application.
